body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\), can one construct a deterministic output-polynomial or polynomial-delay algorithm for the following explicitly charged output? The output must contain one compact arithmetic circuit for each distinct \(g_E\) with \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), where identity means global rational identity on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), the complete list of member states in each identity class, every requested shortest legal-reversal certificate from \(C\), and an exact encoded certificate that the records partition all states in \(\mathcal R(C)\) by functional identity. Total running time is measured against the input encoding plus the total encoding length of all these records; polynomial delay is measured between complete consecutive records and must also account for the record being written. Canonical state enumeration and path-independent partition lifting are already supplied by \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\). The unresolved requirement is deterministic output-sensitive identity and canonicalization for the compact rational circuits after positive-denominator clearing; numerical agreement at finitely many covariance matrices is not an identity certificate.
body.justification: After state enumeration is solved, a meaningful output-sensitive effect problem must charge complete class records, including memberships, certificates, and compact rational representatives.
body.gap: Neither PDAG enumeration nor known-graph effect estimation supplies deterministic output-polynomial or polynomial-delay canonicalization of compact rational circuits under global identity, even after all explicit class-record output is charged.
body.consumer: A solution would let large components feed possible-effect analysis through certified rational-functional classes without hiding member lists or shortest certificates outside the complexity measure.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether the compact rational circuits \(g_E\), for \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), can be partitioned under global identity on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\) by a deterministic algorithm whose total time is polynomial in the input plus the complete explicit output encoding, or whose delay is polynomial between complete class records, with all member lists, exact class certificates, and requested shortest reversal certificates charged to that output.
obligation.obstruction: Positive-denominator clearing reduces equality to multivariate polynomial identity. Full expansion gives a deterministic certificate but can have exponential intermediate size and cancellation relative to the compact circuits and the final class records. Charging all memberships and certificates removes the earlier hidden-output defect, but the frozen core still supplies no deterministic output-sensitive canonical form or identity method controlling this intermediate blow-up.
obligation.attempted: The canonical background-PDAG algorithm closes exact-once state enumeration, path-independent lifting, and shortest legal-reversal certificates. For each pair of compact effect circuits, positive denominators were cleared and numerator coefficient tables were expanded, yielding an exact terminating global-identity test and a finite exhaustive quotient. This proves correctness and termination but not the revised output-sensitive bound.
obligation.partial_result: The state side is closed. By \(\texttt{prop:complete-component-enumeration}\), the canonical background-PDAG procedure enumerates each \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\) once after \(O(p^3)\) initialization, with \(O(p+m)\) delay and output-linear canonical partition lifting. Its transported partitions are path independent. When requested, shortest certificates of length \(\delta(C,E)\) are produced with the safe \(O(p^5)\) per-output bound. On the effect side, \(\texttt{lem:exact-global-rational-effect-identity}\) gives a terminating exact test: clear the positive block-Gram determinant denominators and expand each numerator polynomial, whose coefficient table certifies global identity on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\). Exhausting all states and applying this test produces a finite exact partition, complete member lists, and one representative per rational-functional class. This establishes correctness and termination. It does not establish running time polynomial in the input plus the final complete output encoding, or polynomial delay between complete class records, because intermediate expansions can be exponentially larger than the compact circuits and can undergo cancellations; no deterministic output-sensitive compact-circuit canonicalization bound is available from the frozen core.
